subject: medieval knights
title: The Hundred Years' War Didn't Last a Hundred Years

scenes.text: The Hundred Years' War didn't last a hundred years.
England and France started fighting in thirteen thirty-seven.
They didn't stop for good until fourteen fifty-three. That's a hundred and sixteen years.
And it wasn't even one war. It was a string of wars, broken up by treaties and long truces.
Nobody alive back then called it that. The name was only stuck on centuries later.
So the Hundred Years' War was longer than a hundred years, and not quite a war.

description:
The Hundred Years' War didn't last a hundred years.
The conflict between England and France ran from 1337 to 1453, 116 years, and it was a series of wars broken up by treaties and truces. Historians only gave it its famous name in the 19th century.
What other historical name do you think is misleading?
first_comment: Bonus fact: England kept Calais, its last foothold in France, until 1558. Which famous battle of the war do you know best?
